message_text: Hi, I'm interested in applying for the Fall semester. What are the requirements?
Great question! For Fall admission, you'll need to submit your high school transcripts, SAT/ACT scores, a personal essay, and two letters of recommendation. The deadline is March 15th.
Do you accept the Common App?
Yes, we accept both the Common Application and our own direct application portal. Both are equally considered.
That's really helpful, thanks! One more thing - is there an application fee?
The application fee is $50, but we offer fee waivers for students who qualify for free/reduced lunch programs. You can request one through the Common App.
Perfect, you've been super helpful. I'll start my application today!
Wonderful! Best of luck with your application. Feel free to reach out if you have any other questions.
What immunizations are required for enrollment?
Required immunizations include: MMR (2 doses), Meningococcal (ACWY), Tetanus/Tdap (within 10 years), and COVID-19 vaccination. A TB test is also required.
Where do I upload my immunization records?
Upload them through the Student Health Portal at health.university.edu. Your doctor can also fax records to 555-0199.
What happens if I don't submit them by the deadline?
A health hold will be placed on your account, preventing class registration. The deadline is 30 days before the semester starts.
What clubs and organizations does the university have?
We have over 150 registered student organizations! Categories include academic honor societies, cultural organizations, sports clubs, performing arts, community service, and special interest groups.
Are there any coding or tech clubs?
Yes! We have the Computer Science Club, Hackathon Society, Women in Tech, AI/ML Research Group, and a Game Development Club. All welcome members of any skill level.
Awesome, how do I join?
Visit the Student Involvement Fair during Welcome Week (August 25-27) or browse and join clubs through the CampusConnect app.
That's great info! Really looking forward to getting involved.
That's wonderful to hear! Getting involved on campus is one of the best parts of the college experience.
I got a parking ticket on campus but I have a valid permit. How do I appeal?
You can appeal parking tickets online through the Parking Services portal within 14 days of the ticket date. Upload a photo of your valid permit as evidence.
Where is the parking services portal? I can't find it.
Go to university.edu/parking and click 'Citation Appeal'. You'll need your ticket number and student ID.
Found it. Thanks. This should be easier to find on the main site though.
Agreed, and thank you for the feedback. Good luck with your appeal!
Is there a payment plan available? I can't afford to pay the full semester upfront.
Yes! We offer a monthly payment plan that splits your semester balance into 4 equal payments with no interest.
Where do I sign up for it? I can't find it anywhere on the website.
You can enroll through the Student Portal under Bursar > Payment Plans. There is a $35 enrollment fee per semester.
Another fee... of course. Is there a fee for the fee too?
I understand your frustration with the additional costs. The enrollment fee is a one-time charge per semester.
I just got my acceptance letter! I'm so excited!
Congratulations!! 🎉 We're thrilled to have you join our community! Your next steps are to submit your enrollment deposit by May 1st.
Already submitted it! When is orientation?
New Student Orientation has multiple sessions from June 15 to August 1. You can register for your preferred date through the New Student portal.
Can my parents come too?
Absolutely! We have a concurrent Family Orientation program. Parents/guardians attend separate sessions while you register for classes and connect with fellow students.
This is so well organized. Thank you!
We're so happy you're joining us! See you at orientation! 🎓
When is the FAFSA deadline for next year?
The priority FAFSA deadline is March 1st. Applications submitted after this date will still be considered, but some funds may be limited.
Got it. What kind of scholarships do you offer?
We offer merit-based scholarships (starting at $2,000/year for 3.5+ GPA), need-based grants, departmental scholarships, and athletic scholarships.
I have a 3.7 GPA. Am I automatically considered or do I need to apply separately?
Merit scholarships up to $5,000 are automatically awarded based on your admission application. For larger awards, you'll need to submit the scholarship application by April 1st.
This is great info. The financial aid office here is way more responsive than other schools I've talked to.
Thank you for the kind words! We're here to help. Don't hesitate to reach out if you need anything else.

What's the difference between subsidized and unsubsidized loans?
Subsidized loans don't accrue interest while you're in school at least half-time. Unsubsidized loans begin accruing interest from the disbursement date.
Which one should I take?
Always accept subsidized loans first since they cost less over time. Then use unsubsidized loans only if needed. We recommend borrowing only what you truly need.
Makes sense. How do I accept them in the portal?
Log into the Financial Aid portal, go to 'Awards', and click 'Accept' or 'Decline' next to each loan. You'll also need to complete entrance counseling at studentaid.gov.

Thank you for the kind words! We're here to help. Don't hesitate to reach out if you need anything else.
What are the different dorm options for freshmen?

Freshmen can choose from: Traditional halls (shared rooms, communal bathrooms - $4,200/semester), Suite-style (shared room, private bathroom - $5,100/semester), or Apartment-style (single room, shared kitchen - $5,800/semester).
Can I request a specific roommate?
Yes! Both you and your preferred roommate need to list each other in the housing application. The system will match you automatically.
That's awesome. Do all rooms come with WiFi?
Yes, all residential halls have high-speed WiFi included at no additional cost. Each room also has ethernet ports for wired connections.
Great, this is very clear. Thanks!
You're welcome! Let me know if you have any other housing questions.
I applied 6 weeks ago and still haven't heard anything. This is ridiculous.
I understand your frustration. Typical processing time is 4-6 weeks. Let me look into your application status. Could you share your application ID?
It's APP-29381. I've been checking the portal every day and it still says 'Under Review'.
I see your application. It appears we're still waiting for your official SAT scores to arrive from College Board.
I sent those weeks ago! This is really frustrating. I've been accepted to two other schools already.
I completely understand. Sometimes electronic scores take 3-5 business days. I'll flag your application for priority review once the scores arrive.
Fine. But if I don't hear back by next week I'm withdrawing my application.
I've escalated this to our admissions team. You should receive an update within 3 business days.
The course catalog page keeps crashing on my phone
I'm sorry about that. Our mobile site is being updated. Could you try using a desktop browser or clearing your mobile browser cache?
I shouldn't have to use a desktop to browse a website in 2026. This is terrible UX.
You're absolutely right, and I apologize for the inconvenience. Our web team is working on the mobile responsiveness. Can I help you find what you were looking for in the catalog?
I was trying to look up the class schedule for next semester.
The Spring class schedule is available at university.edu/schedule. Here's a direct link that should work better on mobile.
I need help. what's the difference between in-state and out-of-state tuition?
In-state tuition is $12,500 per year, while out-of-state is $24,000. You may qualify for in-state rates after living in the state for 12 months.
that's a huge difference. is there any way to get in-state sooner?
Students who work at least 20 hours per week in-state can apply for early residency reclassification after 6 months.
ok thats useful info at least, thanks
You're welcome! Visit the Registrar's office for residency reclassification forms.
Can you help me figure out which electives to take for the Business Administration major?
Of course! Popular electives include Digital Marketing (BUS 340), Entrepreneurship (BUS 360), Data Analytics for Business (BUS 375), and Negotiation Strategies (BUS 310).
Which ones are good for someone interested in starting their own business?
I'd recommend Entrepreneurship (BUS 360) and Small Business Finance (BUS 355). Both include real-world project components where you develop a business plan.
Those sound perfect! Are they offered next semester?
BUS 360 is offered every semester, and BUS 355 is offered in Spring. Both still have open seats.
Great recommendations, thanks so much!
Happy to help! Good luck with your studies.
why did tuition go up 8% this year? that's way above inflation
The tuition increase reflects investments in new campus facilities, faculty hiring, and technology infrastructure upgrades. The Board of Trustees approved the increase in April.
that doesnt help students who are already struggling to pay. was there any student input?
The Student Government Association was consulted during the budget process. A student town hall was held in March.
nobody knew about that town hall. the communication at this school is terrible
I understand your frustration. I'll share your feedback about improving communication around tuition decisions. You can also attend SGA meetings which are open to all students.
How do I apply for graduation?
You can apply for graduation through the Student Portal under 'Academics > Apply for Graduation'. The deadline for Spring graduation is February 1st.
Is there a fee?
The graduation fee is $75, which covers your diploma, ceremony participation, and cap and gown rental.
That includes the cap and gown? Nice, my friend at another school had to buy theirs for $60.
Yes, it's all included! You'll receive your cap and gown at the graduation rehearsal.
Does the career center help with resume reviews?
Yes! We offer drop-in resume reviews every Tuesday and Thursday from 1-4pm, or you can schedule a one-on-one appointment with a career counselor.
I'm graduating in December and starting my job search. Any resources for that?
We have several resources: our job board (Handshake), career fairs each semester, mock interview sessions, LinkedIn profile reviews, and alumni networking events.
When is the next career fair?
The Fall Career Fair is September 28th in the Student Center. Over 120 employers are registered. Pre-register on Handshake to get your resume in front of recruiters beforehand.
That's amazing, I had no idea there were so many resources. Thank you!
We're here to help you succeed! Good luck with your job search.
My I-20 hasn't arrived and my visa interview is next week. I'm panicking.
I understand your concern. Let me check the status. Have you submitted all required financial documents?
Yes everything was submitted a month ago. This delay is unacceptable.
I see your documents were received. The I-20 processing has been delayed. I can request an expedited electronic I-20 sent via email.
Why wasn't this done automatically? Other universities sent me their I-20 in a week.
I sincerely apologize for the delay. I'm requesting the expedited I-20 now. You should receive it within 24-48 hours.
Can I bring my car to campus as a freshman?
Freshmen can purchase a parking permit for $450/semester. However, availability is limited and permits are assigned by lottery.
$450 per semester?! That's insane. Is there free parking anywhere?
There is a free park-and-ride lot about 1 mile from campus with a shuttle that runs every 15 minutes during the academic year.
The shuttle is better than nothing I guess. What are the hours?
The shuttle runs Monday-Friday 7am-10pm and Saturday 9am-6pm. It does not run on Sundays or university holidays.
What are the prerequisites for Organic Chemistry?
CHEM 301 (Organic Chemistry I) requires completion of CHEM 101 and CHEM 102 with a grade of C or better.
I got a C- in CHEM 102. Can I still take it?
Unfortunately, a C- does not meet the prerequisite requirement. You would need to retake CHEM 102 and earn a C or better.
OK understood. When is CHEM 102 offered again?
CHEM 102 is offered every Fall and Spring semester, with limited Summer sessions.
Do you require SAT/ACT scores?
We are test-optional for the 2026-2027 admissions cycle. You may submit scores if you feel they strengthen your application, but they are not required.
If I submit them, will low scores hurt me?
If you submit scores, they will be considered as one factor among many. If you feel your scores don't reflect your abilities, you may choose not to submit them.
I can't log into the student portal. It keeps saying invalid credentials.
I'm sorry to hear that. Have you tried resetting your password through the 'Forgot Password' link?
Yes I did that and the reset email never came. I've been waiting 30 minutes.
Please check your spam/junk folder. If it's not there, the email system may be experiencing delays. You can also try the secondary reset option using your student ID and date of birth.
There's no secondary reset option on the page. Are you making things up?
I apologize for the incorrect information. For immediate assistance with login issues, please contact the IT Help Desk at helpdesk@university.edu or call 555-0188.
I need access TODAY to register for classes. This is unacceptable.
I understand the urgency. The IT Help Desk has walk-in hours Monday-Friday 8am-5pm in the Library Building, Room 102. They can reset your credentials on the spot.
What's the acceptance rate this year?
Our current acceptance rate is approximately 62%. We use a holistic admissions process that considers academics, extracurriculars, and personal qualities.
Nice, that's encouraging. What GPA do most accepted students have?
The middle 50% of our admitted students have a GPA between 3.4 and 3.9. However, we consider the full application context.
Awesome, thank you for the info!
You're welcome! Good luck!
How do I set up my student email?
Your student email is automatically created after enrollment. Your email address is firstname.lastname@student.university.edu. Log in at mail.university.edu with your student ID.
What's the default password?
Your default password is your date of birth in MMDDYYYY format. You'll be prompted to change it on first login.
That worked, thanks! But the email interface looks really outdated compared to Gmail.
We're actually transitioning to Google Workspace for Education next semester, which will give you a full Gmail experience with your university email.
Where is the financial aid office located? The website says Miller Hall but there's no building called that on the campus map.
I apologize for the outdated information. Miller Hall was renamed to Student Services Building last year. It's located at the intersection of University Ave and 3rd Street.
That's confusing. The whole website has outdated building names.
You're right, and we appreciate the feedback. The web team is currently updating all campus location references.
Well at least you're aware of it. Thanks for the directions.
Thank you for your patience! The office is open Monday-Friday, 8:30am-4:30pm.
I'm an international student from India. What documents do I need for the F-1 visa?
You'll need: your I-20 form (issued after admission), valid passport, DS-160 confirmation, financial documentation showing ability to cover costs, and SEVIS fee receipt.
When will I receive the I-20?
The I-20 is typically mailed within 2-3 weeks after you submit your enrollment deposit and financial documentation.
Can you also help with housing for international students?
Yes! We have an International Student Housing program with early move-in dates and orientation. The International Student Services office also helps with airport pickup.
That's wonderful. You've been very helpful with all the visa info. Thank you!
My pleasure! Welcome to our university community. Feel free to reach out anytime.

Yes! We have 20 group study rooms and 10 individual quiet rooms. You can reserve them online through the Library portal for up to 3 hours at a time.
Can I reserve one for a group project meeting this Saturday?
Absolutely! Saturday hours are 9am-8pm. Group rooms fit 4-8 people and include a whiteboard and display screen.
That's perfect for our presentation prep. Thanks!
You're welcome! The reservation system is at library.university.edu/rooms.

What meal plan options are available for freshmen?
Freshmen can choose from: Unlimited Plan ($2,400/semester), 14 meals/week ($2,100), or 10 meals/week ($1,800). All plans include $100 in dining dollars for campus cafes.
Can I change my meal plan after the semester starts?
You can change your meal plan within the first two weeks of the semester through the Dining Services portal at no charge.
Good to know. Are there options for students with dietary restrictions?
Yes! All dining halls have vegetarian, vegan, gluten-free, halal, and kosher options daily. You can also meet with our campus dietitian for personalized recommendations.
That's really impressive, most schools don't offer all that. Thanks!
We pride ourselves on inclusive dining! Let me know if you need anything else.
When does the Spring semester start?
The Spring semester begins January 13th, 2027. Move-in for residential students is January 11-12.
When is the last day to drop a class without a W?
The last day to drop without a 'W' appearing on your transcript is January 27th (two weeks after classes begin).
And the last day to withdraw with a W?
The withdrawal deadline is March 28th. After that date, you'll receive a WF (Withdrawal Failing) which impacts your GPA.
I just submitted my application! How long until I hear back?
Congratulations on submitting! You'll receive a confirmation email within 24 hours. Admission decisions are typically sent within 4-6 weeks.
Is there anything else I need to do?
Make sure to: 1) Send official transcripts, 2) Submit SAT/ACT scores if not already sent, 3) Check your applicant portal regularly for any requested documents.
All done already! The application process was actually really smooth.
Wonderful! We're glad to hear that. We'll be in touch soon. Good luck!
I got a scholarship from an outside organization. How do I report it?
Congratulations! You can report outside scholarships through the Financial Aid portal under 'Report Outside Aid'. This is required by federal regulations.
Wait, will it reduce my institutional aid?
Outside scholarships may reduce need-based institutional grants if your total aid exceeds your cost of attendance. However, loans are typically reduced first.
That seems unfair but I guess I get why. Thanks for explaining.
I understand the concern. Our counselors can walk you through exactly how it would affect your package if you'd like to schedule a meeting.
The financial aid section of the portal shows completely different numbers than what my award letter says
I'm sorry for the confusion. The portal sometimes takes 1-2 business days to sync after award letters are sent. Are the numbers higher or lower?
Lower. My award letter says $8,000 in grants but the portal shows $5,500.
That discrepancy should be resolved once the portal updates. If it persists after 48 hours, please contact the Financial Aid office to reconcile the amounts.
So I should just trust the letter and ignore the portal? That doesn't inspire confidence.
I understand your concern. The award letter is the official document. I recommend screenshotting both for your records and following up with Financial Aid if the discrepancy continues.
I'm trying to register for CHEM 201 but it says I have a hold on my account
Account holds can be due to unpaid balances, missing health records, or advising requirements. You can check the specific hold in your Student Portal under 'Account Holds'.
It says 'Advising Hold'. But I already met with my advisor last week!
Sometimes advisors need to manually clear the hold after your meeting. Please contact your academic advisor to confirm they released it.
This is so annoying. Registration closes in 2 hours and my advisor isn't responding to emails.
I understand the urgency. You can also contact the Registrar's office directly at 555-0142. They can help with emergency hold removals during registration periods.
Fine I'll call them. This whole registration system is a nightmare.
I'm sorry for the frustration. I've noted this feedback about the hold removal process.
Your chatbot gave me wrong information last week and I missed a deadline because of it
I'm very sorry to hear that. Could you share what information was provided and which deadline was affected?
It told me the add/drop deadline was February 7th but it was actually January 31st. I missed dropping a class and now I'm stuck with it.

I sincerely apologize for that error. Please contact the Registrar's office and explain the situation. They may be able to process a late drop with documentation of the incorrect information you received.
I'll try but I doubt they'll care. This AI should not be giving out wrong dates.
You're absolutely right, and I'm very sorry. I recommend requesting a meeting with the Registrar's office directly. Reference ticket #INC-2947 for this conversation.
The health portal won't accept my uploaded immunization records. It keeps saying 'invalid format'.
The portal accepts PDF, JPG, and PNG files under 5MB. Could you check the format and size of your file?
It's a PDF and only 200KB. Still getting the error.
I apologize for the technical issue. As a workaround, you can email your records directly to health@university.edu or fax to 555-0199.
Why have an upload portal if it doesn't work?
That's fair feedback. I'll report this bug to our IT team. In the meantime, the email option should process within 1-2 business days.
I'm transferring from community college. How many credits will transfer?
We accept up to 64 transfer credits from accredited institutions. You can use our Transfer Credit Evaluator tool to check specific courses.
I have 72 credits. So 8 of them just disappear?
The 64-credit cap applies to lower-division credits. Some of your courses may count as upper-division equivalents. An advisor can evaluate your specific transcript.
Can I send my transcript now to get an evaluation before I commit?
Yes! Submit unofficial transcripts through the Transfer Student portal for a preliminary evaluation, usually completed within 5 business days.
Ok that's fair. I'll submit them today.
Great! You'll receive the evaluation via email. Feel free to reach out with any follow-up questions.
I've been trying to reach the registrar's office for 3 days. Nobody answers the phone.
I'm sorry about that. The Registrar's office is experiencing high call volumes. You can submit a request through the online ticketing system at registrar.university.edu/help.
I need my enrollment verification letter for my employer ASAP. I can't wait for a ticket.
Enrollment verification letters can actually be requested instantly through the National Student Clearinghouse at studentclearinghouse.org. It's the fastest option.
Oh I didn't know that. Why doesn't the website mention this?
That's a great point. I'll suggest adding this information to our Registrar FAQ page. Thank you for the feedback.
Every section of ENG 101 is full. I NEED this class to graduate on time.

I understand the urgency. You can: 1) Join the waitlist for your preferred section, 2) Check for newly added sections during the first week, or 3) Contact the English department about a capacity override.
There's no waitlist option showing up for me.
The waitlist feature is only available during the registration period. If the period has closed, you'll need to contact the English department directly for an override.
What's their contact info? I can't find a directory anywhere on this site.
The English department can be reached at english@university.edu or 555-0167. Office hours are Monday-Friday, 9am-4pm in Humanities Building, Room 305.
I submitted my housing deposit 3 weeks ago and haven't received room selection access yet.
Room selection access is granted in waves based on deposit date. The next wave opens on May 20th.
May 20th?! All the good rooms will be gone by then. I deposited on April 28th!
I understand your concern. The first wave on May 15th is for deposits received before April 15th. Your April 28th deposit puts you in the second wave.
Nobody mentioned this timeline when I deposited. This whole process is poorly communicated.
I'm sorry for the lack of clarity. I'll pass your feedback to the housing team. You'll still have a good selection of suite-style and apartment rooms available in the second wave.
Can someone explain why the tuition page shows $12,500 but my bill says $14,200?
The $12,500 figure is base tuition only. Your bill may include additional fees such as the technology fee ($350), student activity fee ($200), and lab fees.
Why aren't those listed on the main tuition page? That's super misleading.
I apologize for the confusion. The detailed fee breakdown is available on the Bursar's page. I understand this should be more transparent.
Yeah that's pretty deceptive honestly. Parents are making decisions based on that tuition page number.
Your feedback is noted and I'll pass it along to our web team. In the meantime, you can view the complete cost of attendance at the Financial Aid calculator page.
The online application form keeps timing out and losing my progress. I've tried 4 times now.
I'm very sorry about that technical issue. Are you using the latest version of Chrome, Firefox, or Edge?
I'm using Safari on my Mac.
Safari can sometimes cause issues with our application portal. We recommend using Chrome for the best experience. Also, the application auto-saves every 2 minutes.
It clearly isn't auto-saving because all my essay responses are gone every time.
I apologize for the frustration. I recommend writing your essays in a separate document first, then pasting them in. I'll also report this Safari compatibility issue to our tech team.
I shouldn't have to use workarounds for a university application form. This is 2026.
You're absolutely right. This should work seamlessly on all browsers. I've submitted a high-priority ticket to our development team.
My financial aid package was way less than expected. Who can I talk to about this?
I'm sorry to hear that. You can submit a Financial Aid Appeal through the Student Portal, or schedule a meeting with a financial aid counselor.
I already tried calling the office 3 times and nobody picks up.
I apologize for the difficulty reaching our office. Wait times have been longer during peak season. You can also email finaid@university.edu for a response within 2 business days.
2 business days when my deposit is due tomorrow? That's not helpful.
I understand the urgency. Let me connect you with the emergency aid line. You can also request a deposit deadline extension through the Admissions portal.
I clicked on the housing application link in my acceptance email and it goes to a 404 page
I apologize for the broken link. The housing portal recently moved. The correct URL is university.edu/housing/apply.
How long has this been broken? I bet other students are having the same issue.
Thank you for reporting this. I'll escalate it to our web team immediately to get the link updated in the acceptance email template.
ok. The new link works at least. When is the housing deposit deadline?
The housing deposit of $200 is due by May 1st. Room selection begins May 15th based on deposit date.
excuse me, i applied 6 weeks ago and still haven't heard anything. This is ridiculous.
I understand your frustration. Typical processing time is 4-6 weeks. Let me look into your application status. Could you share your application ID?
It's APP-29381. I've been checking the portal every day and it still says 'Under Review'.
I see your application. It appears we're still waiting for your official SAT scores to arrive from College Board.
I sent those weeks ago! This is really frustrating. I've been accepted to two other schools already.
I completely understand. Sometimes electronic scores take 3-5 business days. I'll flag your application for priority review once the scores arrive.
Fine. But if I don't hear back by next week I'm withdrawing my application.
I've escalated this to our admissions team. You should receive an update within 3 business days.
I was told all my credits would transfer during the campus visit but now admissions says only 45 out of 60 will count
I'm sorry to hear about this discrepancy. The campus visit advisors provide general guidance, while official transfer evaluations are done by the Registrar after reviewing your transcripts.
That's misleading. I chose this school partly because they said all my credits would transfer.
I completely understand your frustration. You can appeal individual credit transfer decisions by providing course syllabi to the relevant department chairs.
How long does the appeal take?
Appeals are typically reviewed within 2-3 weeks. I recommend submitting them as soon as possible before the semester starts.
